answerability: yes: the file describes police-reported motor vehicle crashes and dates, so it can compare average recorded crash counts per calendar occurrence of each weekday in the specified years; it cannot represent crashes not reported to police.
metric: Average number of police-reported crashes per calendar occurrence of each weekday, 2013–2025.
denominator: Number of calendar dates of each weekday in 2013–2025; the numerator is the number of included crashes on that weekday.
population: One record per police-reported motor vehicle crash with a usable crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive.
grouping: Day of week derived from crash_date (Monday through Sunday).
data_check_implications_and_decisions: The check found 2,132,218 dated crashes in the planned years, zero missing or recognized default dates within this population, and complete Jan 1–Dec 31 date coverage in every year from 2013 through 2025. Keep every qualifying row; no qualifying row is dropped or assigned a different weekday. Records without a usable date are outside the date-defined population and cannot be assigned a weekday. The full calendar coverage means each weekday's denominator can be counted across all eligible dates.
limitations: This describes police-reported crashes with usable dates, not every crash that occurred. The check found no missing/default dates within the eligible population and complete calendar-year coverage for all 13 years; this is an average per calendar weekday, not adjusted for time-of-day, travel volume, or exposure.
